Question: Back when women used to be housewives, is it true that they still worked, but only until they were married and/or had children? Was there ever a time women did not work AT ALL?

In the industrial age women's labor was directed to more domestic areas: sewing, weaving, domestic maintenance (housekeeping for others), and in times of war, women were used to replace the men going into the military. Question: What classical music piece has made you cry and why? Has anything else ever had a similar emotional impact on you before or since hearing this piece for the first time?

That fall my church choir was joining with another for an All Saint's Day concert of John Rutter's Requiem, a exquisite piece of music. The last movement features a ethereal soprano solo after which the choir comes in with “they shall rest from their labours…” . The last 16 measures rip my heart out with “Requiem aeterna. “Dona ais Requiem, et lux Perpetua luche at ais…” rest eternal grant them, and light perpetual shine upon them. Powerful stuff. That year, All Saint's Day was November 5th. 6 months to the day after I lost my dad. The program opened with the hymn For All The Saints, and the notes stuck in my throat. I managed to pull it together up to the last movement and the dam burst. I wept hard through the last 16 measures. I've sung the Requiem several times since and I have never been able to sing the last measures. I was telling a friend what a blubbering mess I had been. She shared that a person that can connect so deeply to a piece of music, art, or literature is truly fortunate. They become part of the fabric of the creative art. I like that thought.

Question: I am bothered by something my teacher said to me 12 years ago. I have not seen her in 12 years. Should I let her ruin my life?
Answer: Of course you shouldn't let it ruin your life! Either see a therapist to figure out why you're obsessing about a 12 year old comment, or figure out if there might be some merit to the teacher's comment.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What are the potential consequences of receiving a poor letter of recommendation from an academic advisor?
Answer: Generally, if the professor feels they can't write a positive recommendation, they will decline your request. If a negative recommendation is written, chances are you'll never know. Every recommendation I’ve ever written has been sent directly to the school without the requesting party ever seeing what I’ve written.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Do you agree with Abbe Lowell's statement that if Hunter Biden's last name was not Biden, he would not be facing charges in Delaware and California?
Answer: 100%. I've read that the number of cases like this that are investigated, much less prosecuted is infinitesimally small. Most, if caught, plead out with minimal jail time or a simple fine.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it okay for my boyfriend to just demand to look at my phone?
Answer: No, it's not OK. It means he doesn't trust you, is trying to control you, and isolate you from friends and family. Run. Run far, and don't look back.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What happens if you never pick your children up from school (e.g., you have no family or friends and you just disappeared whilst your kids were at school)?
Answer: Let me see if I have this right: you want to ABANDON your children at school?!? If no one shows up at the end of the day this is what will happen. To even imagine such a despicable act disgusts me beyond words.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Most people talk about how many days they get off a year, teachers talk about how many months they get off. Are there any other professions that get as much vacation as teachers?
Answer: Teachers get the summer off only on paper. They either are taking classes themselves to keep their skill sharp or reach the next pay or academic degree, reviewing curriculum or programs for the next year, teaching summer school, or working a second job to cover expenses. Then there's the whole tending to life they put on hold during the school year: doctor's appointments, car and house maintenance, caring for their own children… and MAYBE we get a week or two vacation.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How did three teenage friends from Texas grow up to become Broadway stars?
Answer: They worked their butts off, practiced, prepared, trained, did regional theater, went to New York, auditioned, studied some more, wash rinse, repeat, then add a large dash of luck.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How should a teacher handle a situation where they ask the class if anyone dislikes them?
Answer: Why on earth would you ask that?!? First, you're not there to be “liked", to bevtheir buddy. You're there to teach. Second, if you asking teens, they are all going to say they don't like you. That's just the nature of the beast. If you need a friend, get a cat or dog.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: As a teen who smokes cigarettes, how do I politely light up a cigarette when people frown, lecture, and judge me when I just need a cigarette and want to smoke in peace?
Answer: I might frown, but I won't lecture, I'd just walk away judging you 12 ways to Sunday, thinking what a moron you are. You can have all the “peace" you want.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: I never talked to my professor or participated in class. I took longer on the final exam on purpose and I was alone with her. She did not walk out with me or hold my hand. Was she rude?
Answer: Was she rude? No,. We're you being weird? Oh yeah! I don't know just exactly what you were expecting, but she was your TEACHER, not your MOMMY. Grow up and get over yourself.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: All my friends who smoke cigarettes now have quit all sports. We hang around coughing and spitting just to satisfy cravings. As a teen, how can I try to quit without my friends thinking I'm dumb?
Answer: Wanting to quit makes you the veritable rocket scientist in your group. Go ahead and quit. You can always find new friends. If they continue smoking, you'll have to do that anyway.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What should I do with my friend who keeps questioning my academic pursuit? She keeps making remarks like "Are you sure you want that university?" Or "You should choose something better". Btw she is struggling with making her own choice.
Answer: Ignore them. Your friend is doing what's call projecting. She's anxious about her choices and thinks or wants others to feel that same anxiety. The summer between my junior/senior years in high school I attended a summer music camp. I had researched the school, the campus and the area in general. I loved it all. I applied immediately and got my acceptance letter in late September, the first in my class to be accepted. My friend kept telling me I should have a “back-up school". Why? I was already accepted. I was endlessly questioned about my choice of majors, the major I had prepared for for years. I knew where I was going, and what I was going to do once I got there. I regretted nothing. My friends on the other hand, changed majors, schools, careers. Just keep your eye on the prize and block the static from others. You'll be fine.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: I'm 16 and I smoke. I started coughing during a moment of silence at church. Do you think people know I'm a smoker?
Answer: Sweetheart, the minute you walked by them, they knew you were a smoker. Smokers STINK! The cough is just the icing on the cake. Take the hint and quit now.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How should a teacher respond if they make a mistake in front of the whole class and everyone laughs at them?
Answer: Laugh with them, of course. What better way to show your humanity, humility, fallibility, and grace?

Name: Karen Neff
Question: As a senior person, do you think extremely old people (90s/100s) at some point get to go “my time’s up” & calmly wait for the end (as they stop usual activities like driving), or the will to keep living on stays the same no matter how old you get?
Answer: My dear aunt had a series of serious falls. The last broke her hip and landed her in a rehab/nursing home at 95. Her mind was as sharp as ever, but her hearing was going and rehab was not to her liking. Swallowing was difficult so her food was liquefied. The only food she enjoyed was the strawberry sundaes her daughter brought. On her 96th birthday, one of her nieces asked what she'd like for her birthday. Her reply was she'd like to not be here. The next day, after lunch she took a nap and her wish came true.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it considered appropriate to use exclamation points in formal emails?
Answer: I had to laugh at this. My husband edited our church's newsletter. He found a large, red exclamation point somewhere, and at the monthly staff meeting, he hand it out to the person whose submission contained the most exclamation points, which he edited out. Leave them out, unless your formal email is announcing the building is on fire.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it possible for a school to deny a senior class's request for caps and gowns?
Answer: I graduated from high school in 1976, the Bicentennial. Everything, and I mean EVERYTHING was red, white and blue. My school colors were blue and gold. Our robes were blue for the guys and white for the girls. Our tassels were either a combination of blue and white, or the individual colors. The week before graduation, we get our caps and gowns. The company sent RED, WHITE, AND BLUE TASSELS! 176 seniors revolted. We demanded the traditional tassels or no tassels would be worn. With graduation a week away, our advisors boxed up the offending items and drove 5 hours to the company to exchange them, then drive 5 hours back to be back in time to leave for the senior trip. A school can try to deny a cap and gown request, but do you really want a class of graduates refusing to show up for their own party?

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it common for students to wear their own graduation gowns instead of the ones provided by the school? If so, why do some schools not allow this?
Answer: For high school, our caps and gowns were rented. For college we had to buy our own.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How do you react when you meet someone who endorses "old school" teaching methods, like the school executive director who held a box cutter to a student's neck?
Answer: Gosh, I'm pretty old and I don't recall anyone advocating holding a boxcutter to a students neck as an accepted teaching technique. When I think Old School, I think of phonics, real math, memorizing times tables and proper grammar. I also think of students coming to school ready to learn, parents who back the teachers and demand appropriate behavior when their child is in the classroom. How I would react would not be good. That an educator would need to resort to threats of bodily harm to control a situation is further evidence of a society in decline.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Why do people become fat? Do they not see themselves in the mirror?
Answer: Body weight is the product of many things. Actual food intake is just a piece of the puzzle. Bone density, genetics, activity level, metabolic rate all go into how much we weigh. People like you crop up every damn day, throwing your shade at us. You take it upon yourself to judge our shopping carts, restaurant orders, what we where, how much space we take up in your world. My advice to you is to MYOB. My guess is those Whoppers and fries you suck down after the basketball game with your bros will catch up with you sooner than later.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: I'm 17 and my mom wants me to help cook Thanksgiving dinner and get a job. I told her I'm not going to because I'm a child and she is still saying I will. What should I do?
Answer: I only wish I had been allowed to do more than set the table and stir the gravy. My mother ft I was a kitchen disaster just waiting to happen. Since then, I've become fairly competent in the kitchen, but it's not my natural habitate. My advice to that end is shut up, open your eyes, pitch in and learn. As for the job, I see no issues unless you are heavily involved in after school activities, and even the, summer employment should not be out of the question.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Why is it difficult to remember information given by a lecturer or teacher in class? Are there any strategies to improve memory retention in this situation?
Answer: Pinning the information on something you already know is one tip. I was taking a class on the Natives of North America. The tribes were divided into 6 regions, with 10 or 12 tribes per region. I was taking a percussion class at the time and needed to know dozens of rudiments. I put the two together, saying all the tribes to a rhythmic pattern related to the rudiments, so as I practiced the rudiments I also recited the tribes by regions. While taking the midterm I'm tapping my foot and bobbing my head. The professor quietly came to me and asked what I was doing. “Remembering" was my answer. I was the only person to get a 100 on the test.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How should you respond when a professor gives you an F on an assignment and asks you to redo it?
Answer: Unless you want to fail the course, you say “thank you" and redo the darn project. Right this time.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: If you’re voting for Biden, why?
Answer: There's just something off-putting about voting for a sex offending, election denying, insurrection condoning, security breaching, treaty breaking son of a bitch. Character is everything. Biden's not perfect, but I trust he stands for what's best for this country.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Can a person without children ever realise the joy of having them without ever experiencing it?
Answer: I taught for 31 years. Those WERE my kids. Over 1000 kids have walked into my classroom. I did my best to give each of them what they needed, beyond music. I paid for summer camps, new instruments, shoes, lunches. I offered encouragement, corrections, cheered at their successes and mourned their losses. I gave advice and listened to their fears. I'm still friends with many of them. They are all special in their own way. I've shared with them how special they are and were to me. Yeah, I think I got the best of all worlds.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How would you react if you were a student who was forcibly attending classes during summer vacation?
Answer: I'd know it was my own fault for f'ing up during the regular school year.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What are some reasons why some people may not be affected by being yelled at by authority figures such as parents, teachers, or bosses?
Answer: Yelling at a child, subordinate, or clerk simply doing their job is a sign of weakness and lack of control by the yelled. It's a form of intimidation and useless as a means of adjusting behavior. That some individuals don't respond or aren't affected by yelling means either they hear it all the time and it's simply more background noise, or they recognize you for the out-of-control fool you are.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: I have taken many classes where I did every assignment and earned an A, yet I barely remember anything I was taught. Is this normal, or am I doing something wrong?
Answer: For knowledge to stick it must be used… often. It's like muscle memory. The more it's repeated, the more firmly it is ingrained in our memory. It's the use it or lose it thing.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Do you think that winning American Idol is a guarantee of a future career in the music industry?
Answer: Kelly Clarkson, Carrie Underwood, Fantasia, Jennifer Hudson. I realize they all didn't “win", but those are the only participants, winners or otherwise, I can name. As a musician myself, I equate American Idol, AGT, and any other “talent show", with karaoke night at the local bar.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How should one respond to a teacher who says "I am not mad, just disappointed"?
Answer: I cried. I was taking beginners lessons on French horn. I started like a house on fire, but as what usually happens, about halfway through the year I started to slack off. After a couple of lackluster lessons, Mr. B sat and quietly said how disappointed he was in me. He instinctively understood yelling at me was useless. He went the quiet, calm route which shamed me to the core. I was the A student. No teacher was ever disappointed in me. I went home and practiced like mad. He was never disappointed in me again.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What do you find frustrating about teaching?
Answer: 3 things: Parents, Administrators, Politicians. Most parents are great. Supportive of teachers, hold their children accountable, and hold high expectations for them. Then there are the others. Those who think little Johnny poops gold bricks and can't POSSIBLY be the terror the teacher is claiming. The parent expects the teacher to not only educate their charming turd blossom, but give them discipline, which the parent hasn't or won't do. I've known teachers who had kids coming into kindergarten not being potty trained, not knowing how to use a fork or spoon, hold a crayon, sit still, or follow the simplest directions. Then they bitch when the teacher tries to impose structure because the teacher is sqashing their angels creativity. Administrators, and I lump school boards into this, are responsible for the actual running of the schools. The board is made up of people who may or may not have real, practical knowledge of how a public school operates. They are people who are financially able to afford the filing fees and campaign material, and have friends willing to vote for them. In my former district, at least half the board hadn't left the county in years. Their philosophy was “it was good enough for me, it's good enough for my kids”, or more likely grandkids. The actual school administrators hated the actually art of teaching that they got an principals certificate so they can live out their fantasies of power and control. In my 31 years, I've had over 25 principals. I can honestly say there were only 2 or 3 who could be called effective, supportive leaders. Lastly, Politicians. If school boards, who might actually KNOW a public school teacher, politicians have isolated and insulated themselves to the point that teachers are those little people they pass on their way to the Country Club. They mandate testing, set score goals arbitrarily, cut funding, add layers of non-educational hoops for teachers to jump through, create class requirements that treat all students the same regardless of their career goals or educational needs, and don't fund ANY OF IT.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How do old high school teachers feel when they see their former students' accomplishments? Do they feel proud, happy, or jealous of their success?
Answer: I cheer for each and every success my former students experience. I see myself as a pebble thrown into a pond. The ripples expand and touch other ripples, changing the surface of the water. Every life I touch touches how many more lives? What could be better?

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Does being an atheist make people hateful, or does being hateful turn people to atheism?
Answer: Two of the most hateful,hate filled people I know are strict, devout Southern Baptists. Conversely, the 2 atheists I knew were kind, generous of spirit, and accepting of all. Oh, I'm sorry. You were saying…

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Why are Boomers so vehemently opposed to student loan forgiveness?
Answer: 1000 years ago, when I was in college, my freshman YEAR cost LESS than $1500! That included, room, classes, fees for instrumental lessons and student fees. Same schooltoday, for out of state students (like me) is $14,250 tuition, $320 student fees, $8942 for food and housing. State and federal governments contributed to college and university budgets at a much higher rate than they do today. That help keep costs reasonable. Then came Reagan. He cut federal funding to higher education. That funding had to be made up from somewhere. The most obvious being the students. Then, the schools realized industry and pharmaceutical companies would pay them for research, yanking the best and brightest from the classroom, leaving associate, untenured professors to do the actual work of teaching. The schools started cutting teaching position to devote more time and money to research. Add in the predatory lending practice of banks, and other lending institutions, credit card companies, etc… and you've created a recipe for disaster. This is one Boomer who stands firmly in the corner of student loan forgiveness in part or whole.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Why did I stop socializing after turning 19? I was fine in middle school. I had friends, but now in high school, I can’t even make eye contact with people. What’s wrong with me? Am I autistic?
Answer: While I'm in no position to diagnose anyone's anything, I will say I went through a similar phase in high school, especially during my senior year. I pulled away from everyone the last half of the year. Maybe it was a self-defense mechanism. Big changes were coming. Painful changes. I'd be leaving all my friends, family, everything familiar when I traveled over 500 miles to attend university. You may be experiencing the same transitional phase. Growth is hard and can be painful. I recommend spending some time getting comfortable with yourself. Really examine who you are, what your interests and talents are, and where you want them to take you. There's a great song by Jane Oliver called Right Garden. You need to find the right garden for you to grow into your potential.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it possible to develop an allergy to secondhand cigarette smoke if you are not allergic to cigarettes but are allergic to tobacco and other plants?
Answer: Absolutely. My parents were heavy smokers. I had a perpetual sinus infection throughout my youth and adolescence. I moved out to attend college and almost overnight, my head cleared up. Every time I went home *bam* sinus infection. If I spend any time around smokers, I come away with a raging headache. I avoid smokers like the plague.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Can being a teacher negatively affect one's personal life, such as their social life?
Answer: As with many things, it depends. I was working at my dream job. I was teaching beginning band. Life was very good. My husband and I purchased a cute house, and had decided to start our family, then the rug was pulled out from my feet. The district had built a new, consolidated high school, which meant a major staff shake up through out. I got moved to the small, unconsolidated high school 50 miles from my home. I had just started fertility treatments and this new position meant I would be leaving home before 6 am, from August-November I wouldn't be getting home before 6 pm because of marching band, my husband had just taken on an added job as a community choir director so he was away until after 10 on some nights… it was all too much and something had to give. That something was having children. I stayed at that band position for 19 years. Many of those kids became MY kids. They needed me to be there in ways that wouldn't have been possible if I'd had children of my own. There are kids who went to college because of me, kids who didn't commit suicide because I was there, kids who saw life in different ways because of me. Ultimately, I've come to believe I was where I needed to be. So,I could look as my career as a negative that created a lot of positives.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: A girl has destroyed my life in college. She is leading her life in a good way and I’m suffering everyday. I am searching for a black magic practitioner. What should I do?
Answer: If your life has been “destroyed" it's probably your own fault, not hers. What you should do is get your own act together, put her in your rear-view mirror, change schools if you must. Just get on with your own life.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Ladies: Do you feel safer when you have a man next to you?
Answer: Depends on the man and circumstances. Husband: yes Cousins/Uncles: yes In a public place like store or theater: usually Stranger on the street: often no.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Can parents legally kick their child out the day they turn 18?
Answer: Your question is regarding the legality of kicking a child out of the house at 18, not the appropriateness. In the US, 18 is the age of majority, so yes, I've known parents who legally kicked their daughters out at their 18th birthday. One of them turned 18 on August 1st, just before the start of her senior year. She had nowhere to go, so she moved in with, you guessed it, the pedophile who'd been grooming her for years. She dropped out, and it took her 10 years to get her GED. Personally, I think kicking your child out before graduation, without any or limited means of support is cruel. I could get behind setting up a plan to lead them toward independence, or add responsibilities within the household, but that has been that child's home/refuge for 18 years, and to be summarily removed because of a birthday says volumes about what sort of person YOU are, and ain't none of it good.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: If Trump was not such an awful man, could you support his policies?
Answer: If he wasn't such a disgusting, despicable human, he wouldn't have such reprehensible policies.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What do you say to someone who has been cast as the lead role in a musical theater performance but is constantly nervous before performances and forgets their lines, etc.?
Answer: Rehearsal, Rehearsal, Rehearsal. The words and music half to become second nature. Rehearsal help. Repetition helps. Focusing on your other cast members help. Otherwise, you can, and should be replaced. I once did a production of Evita. The Che character actor REFUSED to sing a particular line correctly as “17 October, 1945. He did it the American way, , October 17th ,1945. He pulled that crap once too often and the director had him replaced THE NEXT DAY! There will always be someone who wants the part more.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Do professors prefer to be asked for letters of recommendation through email or in person? What factors influence their decision?
Answer: ALWAYS face to face. That way you can answer any questions they have regarding the school, your future plans, extra curricular activities applicable to your recommendation… etc.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it considered appropriate to use "Dear Sirs" in an email or letter addressed to multiple recipients, even if not all of them have been identified personally?
Answer: I would say NO, because in this day and age, in most western countries, they probably aren't all “sirs". “Dear sirs and madams", while awkward might be more accurate. Or even, “To Whom it May Concern".

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it necessary to ask someone if they will write a strong recommendation before asking them to be your recommender? Why or why not?
Answer: Reread your question. It's redundant. Just ask if they would write you a recommendation. Don't ask if you can ask, which is what your question says.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Should I see the Broadway production of 'Godspell' before it closes?
Answer: I thought it was a great show, but it's no longer on Broadway. Check around. I'm sure you can find a local production, especially around Easter.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How have anti-smoking laws affected your experience at bar/restaurants with non-smoking sections as a smoker?
Answer: My parents were heavy smokers, and died early as a result. Growing up in that household, I had a perpetual sinus infection and if I got a cold, it inevitably turned to bronchitis. For that reason, I am vehemently anti-smoking. I hated eating in restaurants that didn't have a non-smoking area. Since the enacting of anti-smoking laws, dining out has been so much more pleasant. As I reread your question, I realized you were asking for a smokers perspective. Sorry, I care not one whit about how people who can't kick that nasty, filthy, foul smelling, disgusting, deadly habit think.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it rude to smoke on a date if your date is a non-smoker?
Answer: If my date lit up during our date, that date would be instantly over. That's assuming I didn't know he smoked in the first place. If I knew he was a smoker, I wouldn't have accepted the invitation.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Are there any notable female bass singers?

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Were the women from older generation really as unhappy and oppressed as modern feminists report?
Answer: If that's all you've experienced, you don't know any better, or understand there can be a better way. In many ways, I had strong, capable, educated women as examples in my life. Both of my grandmothers had college backgrounds. My maternal grandmother taught for 2 years before marrying, and helped my grandfather run the family dairy farm operation while raising 3 children. My paternal grandmother came from a monied background, controlled the family pursestrings, made and financed all the major household purchases, including cars, was the town’s postmaster, raised (with domestic help) 4 children and 2 grandchildren. Those 2 women were forces to be dealt with. My mother should have assumed as strong a role in the family she and my father created, but she chose the 1940s version and adopted the weak damsel role. She assumed the role of “lesser" in the family, and resented every minute. Where my grandmothers understood what a partnership a healthy marriage could be, mom played down her abilities and resented everyone else, including me, for choosing a different path from her. So to answer your question, some women found ways to work within the gender expectations of there day, and thrive. Others got swallowed up by the weight of it all.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What is the average pension for a retired teacher in California?
Answer: Pension anywhere depends on education level, years of service, and the pay scale in the district where they teach.

Name: Karen Neff

Name: Karen Neff
Question: You have a vision of the person that you want to date or marry. Did it turn out that way?
Answer: Yes, I did. Then I grew up. I got nowhere with my “type", so I boiled my requirements down to 3. No smokers, must be musical (sing, play an instrument), must be educated (at least an undergraduate degree, but advanced degrees preferred. I figured that would weed out the riff raff and allow me to focus on the finer points of character. I married a non-smoking, church musician (organist/choir director), with 2 music degrees. We'll hit 30 years this October.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What is the average teacher's salary after retirement in the United States?
Answer: That answer varies by district, state, years of service, level of education, etc… in short, there is no one answer.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Why do the average Americans retire at 62 years of age instead of 67? Isn’t it better to retire late to get the most out of social security?
Answer: My father died 13 months after retiring at 67. His final piece of advice to me was do not spend your life working. He wanted to travel, explore, and have fun, but a cancer diagnosis stopped all that cold. I retired after 31 years of teaching, at 58. I was sick of the administrative hoops, the paperwork, and the general bull $&%!. I've reconnected with long time friends and family, traveled, started an exercise routine, and enjoying life in general. I have not started collecting SS, and won't for another year. My husband, who retired at 70 and does get SS, and I live comfortably in our own home on his SS and my teachers pension. We have no credit debt, and 1 car payment. We're doing well. Life is short. Get out there and enjoy it.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How do I handle being alone at prom or homecoming, why does it hurt so bad, I have friends but no boys will go with me, am I just not that pretty?
Answer: Did you know desperation has a smell? The pheromones produced by your body telegraph your loneliness. Smile, socialize, shake your groove thing during upbeat songs. Those things will do more to lift your spirits than anything else.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: My boyfriend doesn't cuddle me, hug me, touch me, say I love you or goodnight to me anymore. Is this just a phase or does it mean our relationship is over?
Answer: One reason, that could have nothing to do with you, could be that he just wasn't raised with a lot of physical affection. There wasn't much affectionate touching in my home. That's not to say there wasn't love or other ways affection was shown. Our parents just weren't outwardly demonstrative with regard to touching or kissing. To this day, I have to force myself to hug, kiss, or otherwise show or accept physical affection. Look at his family. Does this describe them? If you need more contact, ask for it in a loving way. If he's still not filling this need, ask yourself if this is something you can live with.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What is the hardest thing for teachers to do?
Answer: I taught music for 31 years. Part of that was teaching concert etiquette. To this day, when I'm at a concert or in a large group, and the main entertainer or speaker comes out, I have to fight the urge to say “Remember your concert manners.”

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How do I write an application to the principal to apologize for their children’s bad behavior in a classroom?
Answer: First, you don't apply to apologize. You offer a sincere and heart-felt “I'm sorry". Second, it's your child who committed the infraction, therefore it should be your child who should be apologizing.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How do bad grades in university affect your academic record if you had good grades in high school?
Answer: Entering college, in essence, resets your grades. You start from 0. Bad grades in college means you might not graduate, you may be overlooked for employment. Not mentioning you'll be up to your armpits in debt.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What was the worst math teacher you had in your high school?
Answer: 2 math teachers spring to mind. First was my 7th grade math teacher. She gave us a quiz every Friday, then on Monday, she rearrange the room by grade. The higher the grade, the closer you sat to the front of the room. Alphabetically, I would have been in the middle of the room, but grade-wise I was seated in the farthest reaches of the room. The result was my grade got even lower. She left after Christmas and Mr. Cannon took over. He was aptly named. He had a big, booming voice that demanded your attention. His seating plan also moved me closer to the front. And it didn't hurt that he was easy on the eye. My grades shot way up. The other was my algebra II teacher. He went over the skill, made the assignment then sat down and read the farm reports. I learned nothing, but somehow passed anyway.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What is the proper etiquette for addressing a principal or teacher by their first name in a message?
Answer: You DON'T unless they've A. Given you permission or B. Have a social relationship outside of school. If you are contacting them in a professional capacity, they should be addressed by Mr., Mrs., or Ms.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it necessary to ask a teacher for a reference letter in order to improve your chances?
Answer: Teachers and professors aren't mind-readers. If we aren't asked, how are we supposed to know what you want or need from us? In either a quite moment or in an email, request a letter of recommendation. Give them specifics as to where the letter is to be directed, list your awards, accomplishments, activities both in and out of school. Anything you think they need to know about your life out of school.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: I’m 12 incontinent, wear diapers 24/7. I’m horrified at school someone mean finds out making me the diaper girl. My grades haven’t dropped but in class now I stand still, worried. I used to participate actively. A teacher asked me why. What can I do?
Answer: Have you seen a doctor regarding your incontinence? There are several medical interventions that can address this issue.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: I make my parents upset, not intentionally. They just dislike my life choices. This is the reason why my siblings hate me. What should I do?
Answer: Are you making smart life choices? I mean, we're not talking about the use of illegal drugs, underage drinking, sneaking out to meet up and party with friends, right. These are some things your parents might have an issue with. If you're over 18, not living at home, attending a school of some sort, or working an honest job, your choices are just that: YOUR CHOICES. Live your best life. As for your siblings, you have no control over their feeling. Hold no animosity toward them. They are probably aping your parents attitude. By living an honorable life, perhaps you can shift their perspective. If not, live your best life.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: As a teen, if I wanted to smoke cigarettes, what would be the best way to talk to my parents and tell them about my decision? My bestfriend is already smoker, and I realize this is a big deal and I can't go back and wont want to quit once I start.
Answer: Why start? Because of a friend? If no one's told you this yet,let me be the first to say THAT'S STUPID! What if you and your friend have a falling out? You'll be minus a friend and left with a disgusting, deadly habit that more and more people shun. If you think you need to mimic everything your friend does in order to remain friends, I seriously rethink that relationship. Just don't start.

Answer: A frontal lobotomy w/electroshock therapy, and a side order of LSD.

Question: What is the most effective way to request letters of recommendation from teachers and professors? Can you provide a sample email as a reference?
Answer: I always requested my recommendations in person. That way, the professor saw me, could get pertinent information (school, contact person, program I'm applying to…), and I could answer any other questions they had. I would simply say “Dr. ____, I'm applying to ABC School of Sword Juggling, and was hoping you'd be willing to write a letter of recommendation?

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What do you call a woman who doesn’t want to be married or have kids?
Answer: I have several friends who fit your criteria: Claudia, Margie, Stacy, … I'd call her by her given/chosen name.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What are the potential drawbacks of being extremely popular in high school? Is popularity always beneficial?
Answer: The “popular" people in my high school generally reached their peak and it was all downhill from there. No matter how big your school, it's miniscule compared to the world you'll be entering upon graduation. Revel too long in that popularity, or depend upon it to carry you through the next chapters of your life and you're going to be one sad, disappointed puppy. Popularity can be a double-edged sword. Yeah, it makes high school life fun, but unless you can translate that popularity into skills to help you through adulthood, it's an anchor that will hold you back.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: I am 5’10 205 pounds, can I play on the D line on my freshman year of high school? I’m not very slow and am quite strong.
Answer: The only way to know is to go to practice, work your butt off and try.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What meal from your childhood did you dread being served?
Answer: The tradition at our home Christmas morning was that my brother and I would be up before the sun, open our stocking and wait for our parents to get up. We had to wait until after breakfast to open everything else. Mom would make a “special" breakfast of either pan cakes or waffles. I HATE pancakes and waffles. She fix our plates loaded to the rafters with those wretched things, covered in butter and syrup. I could choke down one, maybe two if they were small, but she'd just load more on. By this time brother has eaten his weight in these abominations and is raring to tear into the bounty under the tree. Meanwhile, I'm in tears over being forced to clean my plate. I'm 66 years old and can count the times I've chosen to eat pancakes and waffles on one hand.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What do you say to parents who's children behave bad in school and are constantly getting bad grades and the parents say it's the teacher who has to teach them in order for their grades to be high, and their behavior to go down?
Answer: As long as you understand that a child's first teacher are their parents, you aren't wrong.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What are some reasons for parents being rude to teachers about their children's behavior?
Answer: I've seen this happen on numerous occasions. There are several reasons. First, the parent believes their little angels couldn't POSSIBLY be the cause of any issues in the classroom. The kiddo isn't the problem. It's ALWAYS the teacher. Second, if the child DOES misbehave or otherwise fall short, it's seen as an indictment of the adults parenting skills.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: I put my mother, who is in good health, in a nursing home last year. I have just finished selling her house and possessions. Should I now visit her and tell her the good news?
Answer: My mother in law had turned 90. We had suggested many ways that would enable her to SAFELY remain in her home. All of which she declined. After her stroke and subsequent car accident she had because her reaction time was failing, she gave up driving. We drove 6 hours (there and back) to visit every 2 weeks. She finally realized living alone was no long safe and her youngest son took to to view care facilities in her area. She chose a lovely facility with progressive care. In the course of a year and a half she fell three time. Once breaking her nose, one her hip, and last her pelvis. She is currently in skilled nursing and with advanced dementia. My husband (eldest of 4 boys) handles her financials. Her home was sold and the proceeds given to her financial advisor to invest to provide for her continued care. The facility she's in costs $14,000+ a month! She had invested wisely, but her funds are dwindling. In the event she out-lives her money, Medicaid will ensure she stays where she is, receiving proper care. If you haven't already, you need to do as my husband did, and somehow bank her money to pay for her care. To do otherwise is, at the very least, fraud, if not outright theft. Unless that home was in your name, it was her house and the proceeds belong to her. And for mercy sake, GO VISIT YOUR MOTHER!

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What can parents do to make the lives of high school teachers easier during parent-teacher conferences and throughout the year?
Answer: The best thing a parent can do is listen to their child's teacher with an open mind. Don't be defensive. Remember your child's actions are a product of THEIR decisions and not necessarily a reflection on your parenting. It's best to spproach the parent/teacher relationship as collegial, not adversarial. You share the same goal of educating and socializing the child.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Could Trump do a woman on 5th Avenue in the middle of the street? Would anyone care?
Answer: I would sincerely hope that any decent human would be heroic and shoot HIM on 5th Avenue.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it socially acceptable for a woman to have a higher paying job than her husband?
Answer: Pardon me, but who the Hell cares? And what does social acceptance have to do with anything? As long as the couple work together on shared goals, it's nobody's damn business.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: I’m a teacher and the school principal is threatening to fire me because I’ve been smoking cigarettes in front of my pupils. How do I tell him that we live in a free country, & that means that I have the right to do whatever I want?
Answer: Schools are drug free zones. Nicotine is a drug. Some in your school have health conditions aggravated by cigarette smoke. You're lucky it's only a threat. Where I taught, it would have meant immediate dismissal.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it advisable for non-smokers to date individuals who regularly smoke cigarettes, especially if they do not smoke themselves?
Answer: I don't know that “advisable” the word I'd use. My husband used to smoke. Never at his work, which is where I met him. He said he would totally quit for a week or two every summer during a music camp he ran. One year, he decided that if he could quit for a week or two, he could quit for good. He went cold turkey. If I had known he smoked, I doubt I would have been open to a relation with him. My parents were heavy smokers and it killed them. No way was I signing up for that. In my case smoking would have been a deal breaking. I seriously doubt we would have even been friends. I find the smell of most smokers repulsive.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it acceptable to smoke in a shared living space if others do not want the smell of cigarettes?
Answer: It is completely unacceptable to smoke in a space shared with none smokers. Nonsmokers generally find the odor of cigarette smoke disgusting, repulsive, even sickening. If you need to light up, have the desentcy to go outside away from doors and windows, and don't think just because you go into your own space your nasty habit doesn't waft its way into a shared space. It does, and it stinks.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Who was the teacher's favorite student among famous people? Who is considered to have had the worst teacher in history?
Answer: There used to be a saying that went something like only a poor student learns nothing from a bad teacher. Teachers are like shoes, in a way. Not all styles or sizes suit everyone. I've had teachers I adored, that others consigned to the pits of Hell, and vice versa. Get what you can from them, learn on your own by reading. There's more than one way to reach your goals.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How do I get over the fear of loosing my parents? I am 14, and my parents are 51 and 54. They are always under huge amounts of stress, they aren't that active, and don’t eat that well. My biggest biggest fears are losing my parents and growing up.
Answer: I understand your fear. My parents were heavy smokers. I knew from about age 15 that they would miss a large portion of my life due to early deaths. They died when I was 33 and 42. Both of smoking related diseases. First of all, know that them passing before you is all but inevitable. They are 37 and 40 years older than you. Second, you can live with the fear of losing them or enjoy and learn from the years you have them. That includes choosing how to live your life. Lastly, there are no guarantees for any of us. Live your life. Love your parents while you have them. Build memories for after they're gone.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Has a parent ever had their child in one of their classes? How was the experience for both of them?
Answer: One of my music teachers had both his son and daughter in his classes. At one point, I thought it might be nice having your parent as a teacher, but after graduation, I realized the pressure those two were under. They had to be shiny examples of their father's work. The best musicians, stellar behavior, good students, if they so much as burped in class dad heard about it. I suppose it all depends on how the parent handles it. Can they divorce the role of parent from that of teacher? Do they expect more from their children than the average Joe or Jane walking into their classroom? How the adult answers that question says everything.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it possible to skip classes in college without facing consequences?
Answer: I had a world geography class that met at 3 in the afternoon. I went to the first class, picked up the syllabus, realized the professor was less interesting than paint drying and went once out of the 2 or 3 times it met per week. I justified it by telling myself that I had marching band immediately after and needed a change of clothes. I showed up enough to squeak out a C. If you don't mind missing lectures and getting mediocre grades, go ahead a skip.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: I approached my classmate and her dad in high school. She introduced me to her dad and he asked me how I was. I said "good" and walked away. Were they rude?
Answer: Who walked away? You? You were the rude one. The proper response should have been along the lines of a hand shake and a “nice to meet you.”

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Do you think Melania Trump is upset with Donald Trump for mentioning their son Barron's high school graduation in court?
Answer: I care not one whit how Melania feels about anything. The twice impeached, 89 times invited, philandering, misogynistic, homophobic, xenophobic asshat only mentions Barron, or indeed anyone of his children when it serves his purposes. His sole focus is on keeping his behind out of prison.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it possible for someone on the inside of a school or university (such as administration or teachers) to change grades or add classes without getting caught? How difficult would it be to do so?
Answer: Back in the late 70s, my university had a violin student from Iran. After the overthrow of the Shah, the study of music and art was considered anti-revolutionary. Ramen or his family would have suffered severely if the government knew he was continuing his music studies, so the Dean of Humanities worked out a deal that a false transcript was sent to the authorities in Iran. Thus keeping everyone safe.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Did you work during high school? Will you make your kids work?
Answer: I was active in all aspects of music when I was in high school. My brother has his sports. Work outside school was not something that could fit into those schedules. We did some short term stuff in the summer, but that was about it. My brother's 2 children both worked when they were in high school. They're now in their late 30's early 40's. I don't see that those after school jobs did them any good. Neither attended college or trade school. Both work at entry to mid level jobs with little room for advancement. Fat lot of good those extra years of work got them. While I didn't have children, my feelings are that school IS their work. Babysitting, peer tutoring, maybe, but nothing more than a couple of hours a week.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it common for parents to yell at their children due to stress rather than their behavior?
Answer: Of course stress plays a roll. Sadly, that doesn't ease the damage caused to the child. It teaches them that while they aren't allowed to have tantrums, yell, or lash out, it's perfectly acceptable for an adult to do the exact same thing. Additionally, to a child's mind, it makes the child responsible for the happiness of the adult. That's a huge burden for a child to carry into adulthood. In short, an adult needs to recognize their stressor and find constructive ways to release them. Yelling only spreads the stress to little ones who don't understand.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What would happen if the presiding judge in Trump's hush money trial bans him from going to his son's high school graduation, but Trump ignores this and goes anyway? Who wouldn't ignore such an order to go to his son's graduation?
Answer: He hasn't gone to any of his other children's graduation. Why should Barron special? Besides, the judge made no such order, so for now the point is moot.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How would you react if a teacher told you that your child was misbehaving in class? Would you trust the teacher's assessment?
Answer: Having been a teacher, my first instinct would be to believe the teacher. As a parent, I want to hear my child's spin/explanation of the situation. I know kids are good at playing the victim and would go to any extent to avoid punishment. After hearing their side, weighing teacher's version against theirs, depending on the infraction, and its frequency, corrective action would be taken at home.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What are the potential consequences of a high school teacher engaging in inappropriate conduct with a minor student, as seen in the case of Erin Ward in Nebraska?
Answer: A teacher charged with inappropriate contact with a minor, student or not, will first of all be suspended with or without pay. They teaching certificate will be suspended until the case is resolved. The case will then proceed to investigations, charges, court cases, a fine and/or jail time, at which point their teaching credentials will be revoked and the possible lose of pension and retirement benefits.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What is the appropriate response when someone says 'bless your heart'? Are there any other responses that could be used instead of 'thank you'?
Answer: “Bless your heart" is not the blessing you think it is. It's generally a condescending comment, spoken by southern women, to mean you're clearly not smart enough to either understand the situation, or see the ways in which you're wrong. The one exception might be if they find you injured and in need of assistance. I have yet to find a satisfying response to the first case, so I usually give a weak smile and walk away.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What do democrats do when we say “let’s go brandon”?
Answer: Absolutely nothing, except marvel that you manage to walk upright without dragging your knuckles.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What could be the reason for a parent getting mad over small things and having frequent short tempers towards their children?
Answer: For much of my childhood and youth, my mother didn't speak so much as yell at my brother and me. My father worked away from home for much of this time, so mom was the boss. Not a job she handled well. She was lonely, overwhelmed, angry, often depressed, and bored, points I only fully understood after she died. Knowing the reasons for her anger didn't fully mitigate the pains it caused me at the time, but it did give me the ability to find a degree of forgiveness in my heart.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What is the highest paying position in a student council and why is it considered a desirable role?
Answer: Student councils are not paid. The highest position is president and it is an elected position, voted upon by either the the council or the student body.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How was Mozart's talent perceived by his contemporaries? Was he considered on par with Beethoven or even more exceptional, or were his abilities seen as typical for a child prodigy during that time period?
Answer: As Mozart predated Beethoven, you have the comparison backwards. It's said that Beethoven's father tried to market the younger Beethoven to be the next Mozart. I also think you misunderstand what a prodigy is. Prodigies are rare, not springing up like dandelions. They display remarkable talents and gifts, seemingly without effort or training. How Mozart was perceived by his peers can be read on numerous sources.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How can you ask for more teachers in a letter to the principal?
Answer: Principals have very little say in how many teachers fill their building. Those decisions lay squarely with the school board. The board determines the number of teachers any school gets by the number of students in the building. I taught at a very small Jr/Sr high school. Think graduating classes under 30. When I started there we had 2 foreign language teachers, 4 teacher each for English, social studies, and math, 3 science teachers, 2 p.e. teachers, 1 each for art, computers and music. There were also 3 special learning teachers. Now the staff has been halved. Some shared with other buildings. Allocation is all based on student population numbers.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How do I write a letter to my teacher to change the instrument that I’m studying now?
Answer: I've dealt with students switching instruments every year. It was never a big deal and usually after a few extra lessons they were good to go. I recall one student in particular that started on baritone in 6th grade. By Christmas, he was playing in book 2. After Christmas, he came back with his aunt's flute. After a couple of lessons he was zipping along also headed for book 2. Along about Ash Wednesday he wanted something more difficult., so I showed him a bassoon. It was love at first sight. He's earned his PhD in bassoon performance, plays in several orchestras, and had written several compositions for the instrument. All you need to do is ask.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What is the name of the attachment on a trumpet or trombone that produces high notes?
Answer: No special attachments. It's all mouth positioning and air.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is playing the trumpet a good alternative for people who can't sing well? Why or why not?
Answer: I had a student who couldn't carry a tune in a bucket, but put a saxophone in his hands and he could make that thing talk. For a person who can't sing, trumpet would not be my first choice of instrument. Brass and string instruments rely heavily on being able to play pitches by audition, that is, imagining the pitch before you play it, much like visualizing your route before you take a trip. I think clarinet or saxophone would be much easier for you to learn. One fingering=one pitch. With brass, one fingering can get you 8–10 different pitches. Emboucher is everything for pitch. Strings, you have to be able to feel where the pitches fall on the finger board. Just my thoughts.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What is the appropriate way to address tutors or lecturers? Is it acceptable to use their first names or should a title like "professor" be used? How do they prefer to be addressed?
Answer: How ever they introduce themselves is how you should address them.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it possible for a retired government teacher to return to work after receiving pension money and benefits?
Answer: As a retired teacher, I can substitute X number of day in any given school year. The number of days varies from state to state. If I wanted to take another full time teaching job, I would A)bHave to change states. Example: you live in Southern PA. If you had a Maryland or West Virginia teaching certificate, you could work in that state while retaining your PA pension. Or B) Work at a private school that doesn't pay into the state's teacher retirement system. I have friends and family who have done both.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Since trans women and cisgender women are in conflict over trans women sharing bathrooms, what about trans men? Do trans men use male bathrooms? If they do, why have we not heard anything about it?
Answer: No cis woman I know worries about who's using the stall next to them. Interestingly, the people who are freaking out about who's in the women's restrooms are cis men. Perhaps it's false gallantry, or they think they're protecting women-folk. It's all ridiculous.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How would you describe the satisfaction of teachers with their pay?
Answer: Personally speaking, if teaching was the only thing I had to do, my pay would have been OK. Not great, but livable. Unfortunately, teaching increasingly became a side gig after standardized testing, mountains of paperwork, endless meetings that should have been an email, more paperwork, observations, IEP meetings, parent/teacher conferences (where parents were a no-show), more meetings, learning new “techniques and technologies …it got to be ridiculous.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Should 82% of teachers say that the state of public education has gotten worse over the past five years?
Answer: Only 82%? The other 18% are either delusional or liars.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How do you quit drinking alcohol when alcohol is helping you cope?
Answer: It really isn't. It's hiding the problems while adding to them. Far better would be to put down the bottle and get into therapy, a 12 step program, and face your issues with a clear mind.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What is the general perception of smokers among non-smokers? If you could express your thoughts without causing offense, what would you say to non-smokers about smoking?
Answer: “Did you not get the memo? Smoking kills.” “I'm sorry. I can't stand your nicotine stench. Please move away.” I really don't care if my comments are offensive. I've lost both parents, 3 friends, have asthma caused by second hand smoke, and have absolutely no tolerance for this stupid, deadly habit.

Question: What do you do when your cheating boyfriend leaves without any explanation?
Answer: Change the locks, box up his crap, call his mama to come and get it, then thank your lucky stars you dodged that bullet.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: My girlfriend is working 55 hours a week and taking 4 classes at school, how can I help her through this, she’s beyond stressed, and I don’t know how I can help, what should I tell her to do?
Answer: You shouldn't “tell” her anything. Take some things off her plate. Fix her some meals. If you live together, clean your house or apartment. Offer to take her car to the garage for service. Do the grocery shopping. Make her life as easy and smooth running as possible.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: How do teachers typically react when a student has a bad grade in one subject but good grades in all other subjects? Do they suspect cheating as a possible explanation?
Answer: I generally did not know any student's grade in any other class. Having been a student myself, I am well aware that an individual's skill level will vary from subject to subject. Cheating doesn't need to be involved.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Who was Chopin's main love interest? Did he ever get married?
Answer: Frédéric Chopin was engaged to Maria Wodzinska, but they never married. His maintained a long term relationship with Aurore Dupin (pen name George Sand).

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What's the coldest thing a doctor has ever said to you?
Answer: Not nearly as traumatic as some of the other stories, but it still galls me. After years of marching band, standing and walking on concrete floors, and life in general, my dysplastic hips had been reduced to bone on bone. I could not walk, lay down or sit in anything but a La-Z-Boy type chair. I had been given some heavy duty pain killers that only made me sleepy and constipated. I was on medical leave from my teaching position. I finally got in to the orthopedic surgeon associated with the medical practice I had been dealing with. I had to be wheeled in because I physically could not walk the distance from the car to the office. He demands I get on the exam table while he looks at my x-rays. He turns to me, totally straight faced and says “You'll need to lose 100 lbs and gain 25 years before I'll consider hip replacement for you.”. How in He'll am I supposed to lose 100 lbs when I CAN'T MOVE!?! I thought my husband was going to deck him. I was finally referred to Hershey Medical Center. It's been 9 years, I exercise daily, and I actively curse that bastard every chance I get.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Do teachers have favorites among their students? How can one determine which students they favor and what factors contribute to their favoritism?
Answer: Yes, we have favorites. The reasons and qualities vary. Sometimes, we see ourselves in that student, and think about what we needed at that point in our lives. Sometimes they display a gift that needs nurturing. Still other times I've sensed their need for a positive voice in their lives. Sometimes, you just click, speaking the same language, sharing a similar sense of humor. The thing is, though we have favorites, most of us really try not to show it.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Does your housekeeper do your laundry, dishes, and make the beds? Our new housekeeper says she doesn't do that kind of thing.
Answer: The tasks you mention need to be negotiated. If you want them done by a housekeeper you must negotiate an increase in wages for the added labor. If the person currently doing your housekeeping does not want to do these added chores you have two choices. 1. Find a housekeeper who will do these additional chores for a price you're comfortable with or 2. Hire a second person to do the chores.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Do you think that banning social media in Georgia schools could prevent teachers from showing educationally valuable YouTube videos?
Answer: When I taught History of Rock and Roll, YouTube was my go-to resource. Archival videos of early performers like Chuck Berry, Little Richard, the Beatles, societal movements, protest marches, news events gave the students a glimpse at what the world was like back then in ways books and still pictures just didn't or couldn't do. There should be a way to give teachers pass codes to access this material, while limiting the students. Facebook, Instagram, TicToc etc… on the other hand have no place in a classroom.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Have you ever seen someone get distracted or messed up by music playing in the background while playing a sport?
Answer: That would be me. Not in a sports setting, but in life in general. If music is playing while I drive, I have to turn it off if I'm in traffic. If I'm exercising, the exercise better be with the beat or I flail about like a fish out of water. I just get lost in the words and/or music.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: As a teacher, what is your ‘they never taught THIS in school’ moment?
Answer: After reading a few sadly serious answers, here's a funny one. For my Teaching Elementary School Music class, we were sent out to the county hinterland schools to conduct music classes. During my first class (3rd grade), I'm walking around the room singing and shaking the students’ hands. I come to one kid who is literally twirling a REAL pistol around his finger (might have been a BB pistol, but I either way…). I keep singing, but come up behind him, and mid-twirl, snatch it off his finger. The classroom teacher met me at the end of the aisle and relieved me of the gun. I continued with the class. Her review of my handling of the situation was priceless. My supervising teacher on campus used my experience for years. This was 1978.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: What is the experience like for a colonoscopy if you are unable to eat or drink beforehand?
Answer: It wasn't bad. You can have Popsicles, jello, broth, and apple juice, so you won't starve. For me, the worst part was the IV. I have veins that are hard to find, and they always have trouble setting a line. Beyond that, it was a piece of cake.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it rude for me to tell my doctor I won't get a colonoscopy and say why I won't do so?
Answer: Rude, no. Stupid? You betcha. My stepson, with a family history of colon cancer, refused to do basic health care for himself. He died, at 40, with a colostomy bag, of colon cancer that could have been detected with this test.

Name: Karen Neff
Question: Is it okay for parents to let their toddlers wear pull-ups instead of diapers if the child is potty trained?
Answer: I was potty trained before my brother was born in 1960. I was 2. There was no such thing as pull-ups. There was just thicker panties. I remember dressing myself (tee shirt/panties) in the morning. If the kiddo is potty trained, I say go for it. And before anyone calls BS, remember this: memory comes with speech. I spoke clearly before he was born. I was surrounded by adults and older teens, none of whom spoke “baby talk". I remember my 2nd birthday, climbing behind my mother's knees as she lay on her side after lunch. I remember my older cousin's high school graduation (I took my nap under a picnic table). I remember sleeping in the crib and having nightmares.

Question: Why was Anne Boleyn executed and Catherine of Aragon not? They both gave birth to a daughter. Why didn't Henry do the same thing he did to Anne to Catherine?
Answer: The issue was not the birthing of female children. The problem was Anne was a pawn in her family's social climbing endeavors, was a bit of a scold, and through palace intrigue, was accused of adultery. She was pregnant several times in her brief marriage to Henry, but after giving birth to Elizabeth, was unable to carry any to delivery. Henry was desperate for a male heir, and the Seymore family, rivals of the Bolyn's basically threw their daughter/sister at the king as a way to give him his son. Catherine of Aragon was the daughter of Ferdinand and Isabella of Spain, a major rival of England. Catherine had been wedded to Henry's brother who died shortly after the marriage. To maintain the peace between England and Spain, it was decided Henry would replace his brother in the marriage bed. It's said they truly loved each other, but again, though she was pregnant several times over the course of their fairly long marriage but never again had a live birth after Mary. To maintain the peace between the 2 countries, Henry's solution was divorce, but being Catholic, that had to be approved by the Pope, who refused to even consider the petitions. Henry exiled Catherine to Kimbolton until her death.

Question: Why don't teachers like substitute teachers?
Answer: Music is a specific skill that most of us have studied for years. When I needed a sub, it would have been ideal if they knew music: how to read it, direct it, explain it. Most of my subs only knew scores as they related to sports. Therefore I needed to create plans that anybody could decipher, but still stay true to my long-term goal. Band had listening plans, choir had CD's to sing to (provided the sub could work the CD player.) The other classes had related reading or films to watch. I usually gave specific start and stop points for the films, with questions to be answered along the way. 9 times out of ten the subs would screw up the start/stop points and just let the films run. The subs wouldn't do active readings in the classes and the kids “read to themselves" i.e. not read the sections. I even had one sub who “didn't like my plans" go through my libraries and pull totally different material! I'd crawl across a field of glass before I'd take a day off.

Question: What is the reason behind the power of teachers' unions and why do some republicans have negative views towards them? Is it justifiable to hold such strong feelings towards teacher's unions?

Of course, non-music classes: Comp, history, Psych, science and math were all 3 hour c.h. I frequently carried 12–15 credit hours a semester. My sister in law was an elementary education major. Almost all of her classes were 3 c.h. She took 4, maybe 5 classes a semester to my 7 or 9.

Question: Have you ever seen a teacher just lose it in class and meltdown?

Question: Would you consider the war between liberals and conservatives a war between the elites and the people?
Answer: What constitutes “elite" and “the people"? Both my parents, born in the 1920s, came form generational wealth, both monetarily and in real estate. Despite that head start, my parents were solidly middle class. Dad was an electrician, while mom was a SAHM. Because of my grandparents, I got 2 college degrees and a house in a quaint small town. I retired at 58 with a pension and health insurance. By some definition, I am an “elite", though I consider myself part of “the people". I am extremely liberal: pro-choice, LBGTQ+ ally, solid Democrat voter, for sane gun laws, etc … What does “liberal and “conservative“ mean to you? In bygone days, those terms were ways to interpret the Constitution. Liberal seeing the document as a living blueprint for governance. Open to reinterpretation based on changing science and information. Conservative interpretation meant the Constitution was written in stone, what was written was what was meant. Today, I don't think those definitions apply. Liberals want what benefits the most people, fair taxation of the wealthy, improved infrastructure, health care for all, respect for individual bodily autonomy, etc… Conservatives, in my humble opinion, want the opposite: kowtow to the ultra rich with outrageous tax credits, cutting benefits for the needy, inferior education delivered by unfunded public schools, keeping women at the mercy of biology and men… I know which side I'm on.

Question: Is a music teacher allowed to take away a student's credit due to missing a performance because of a family vacation (something that the school considers an excused absence)?
Answer: This happened to me once. We had been working toward a spring choral concert. Now, concert scheduling happens in September for the entire year because we don't want to conflict with sports or class trips, so the earlier we get scheduled the greater ther chance we'll get the dates we want. Additionally, I can send out notifications to the parents of pertainate dates. I selected one particular song for the spring concert especially for my senior soprano. We rehearsed and things are going well. I'm reminding the kids of concert dates. Not a peep. 3 weeks before the concert, while were rehearsing said song, the solo part comes up and she says, like she just realizes it, her father is taking her on vacation that week. WHAT?!? Even knowing the dates for performances months in advance, he decided to pull her out of school during the 1 week when we have performances?!? She wasn't apologetic in the least. In fact, she asked me to change the dates for her. Instead, I gave the solo to her younger sister, right then and there. Little sister nailed it. Big sister was p*ssed! Because the trip was approved by the office, I couldn't touch her grade, but I had several awards, some monetary, to hand out at the end of the year. Guess who was immediately removed from consideration? Guess who was insulted by my oversite? Guess who didn't give a f*ck?

Question: What are the main differences between the way that Conservatoires and universities each time Music as a study? Furthermore, how would these differences lead to better careers in different areas of the music industry?
Answer: Years ago, one of my colleagues was a graduate of a small conservatory in the Shenandoah Valley. I graduated with essentially the same degree from an accredited university in Kentucky. We were discussing our college experiences and classes. Aside from Composition (English) classes, all her classes were music and the teaching thereof related. I had to take classes from each of the different schools: science and math, humanities, phys Ed, history and sociology, on top of the education classes in support of my degree and music classes. While she had more advanced skills on some areas, she had no depth of knowledge in the other, broader areas outside music. That, to me is the difference between conservatory vs. university educations.
